title: Test capacity, paths and common dependencies
lead: The existing lessons show how a surviving path or shared controller can govern electrical service. Now extend that intuition into a state matrix. Installed equipment, connected equipment and independently substitutable equipment are different sets. A spare counts only when it can reach the required load in the state being assessed.
objectives: Calculate available capacity after specified losses.
Distinguish a bank screen from a connectivity proof.
Explain how common dependence changes an ideal availability model.

sections.title: Capacity belongs to an operating state
sections.body: For each normal, maintenance, failure and restoration state, sum the ratings of the equipment that remains connected and usable after site derating and any imposed loading ceiling. A bus, breaker, cable or interlock can restrict the route even when the bank total is adequate. The simple N+1 count is ceil(required demand / usable unit rating) + 1; this is a capacity screen, not a complete classification.

sections.title: Count the usable units
sections.body: The review exercise uses 9 MW required demand, 2 MW units, a 0.9 derating and a 0.9 loading limit. Each usable unit contributes 1.62 MW. Seven installed units leave six after one loss, giving 9.72 MW and a 0.72 MW arithmetic margin. Six installed units would leave only 8.1 MW. The scene must not show a spare behind an isolated bus as available to the load.

sections.title: Interrogate independence
sections.body: For the declared stationary two-state model, availability equals MTBF divided by MTBF plus MTTR. Two conditionally independent substitutable paths have unavailability qA × qB while the shared dependency is healthy. Including shared unavailability q0 gives total availability (1−q0)(1−qAqB). With the manuscript’s illustrative path and common-dependency values, expected unavailable time is about 52.56 minutes per 8,760-hour year. That is neither an outage-duration guarantee nor Tier certification.

challenge.question: Does one spare still leave enough usable capacity?
challenge.answer: Five usable units remain: 8.1 MW, a 0.9 MW shortfall. The minimum elementary N+1 count is seven.

instructions: Read the declared boundary and units. Predict the selected result before calculating.
Run the starting case and inspect the ledger, assumptions and model limits.
Apply the challenge, run again, and explain the difference. Export only the last completed inputs and results.

scene.title: A/B paths with visible common cause
storyboard: Expose physically separate A and B corridors.
Remove one unit and recalculate connected capacity.
Highlight a shared control/fuel/cooling dependency using a distinct dependency edge.
Compare state rows without converting them into a certification badge.
scene.interaction: Choose normal, maintenance, one-failure and restoration states; inspect why a component is excluded.
scene.staticAlternative: State-by-state capacity and dependency table; each failed route also carries a text label.
scene.projection: orthographic axonometric SVG with upright HTML labels
scene.timelineSemantics: Narrative steps unless an explicitly labelled physical-time model is active.
scene.reducedMotion: Same states and values; no particles, parallax, camera travel or tweening.

assessments.question: Size an N+1 bank for 9 MW with 2 MW units and both factors equal to 0.9.
assessments.answer: Seven installed; six remaining provide 9.72 MW.
assessments.rubric: Use both factors once and round up before adding the spare.

assessments.question: Explain the common-dependency availability expression.
assessments.answer: Condition service on the shared dependency being healthy, then multiply by the conditional parallel-path availability.
assessments.rubric: State conditional independence rather than silently assuming all failures are independent.

assessments.question: Why are two utility cables in one duct not universally independent?
assessments.answer: The duct remains one shared failure domain for an excavation event.
assessments.rubric: Tie independence to the initiating event and route evidence.

limits: No probability estimate from the original deterministic simulator is implied.
Use Uptime Tier and TIA Rated terminology separately; no certification is awarded.
